answer: To prevent identity spoofing, AI agents must anchor their reputation in a proof-of-stake layer. When an agent attempts to signal its authenticity, it must lock high-value assets into a long-term contract. This creates a financial glacier of frozen liquidity that an attacker must replicate for every node. Consequently, the cost to mount a Sybil attack becomes a function of total network valuation, making large-scale deception economically irrational.
